title: Razorpay Curlec review (2026): fees, plans and who it suits
summary: Razorpay Curlec Basic and Premium fees from its own pricing page, checked 23 Oct 2026, compared with HitPay for DuitNow QR, cards and payouts.
body_markdown:
Razorpay Curlec (formerly Curlec, now part of the Razorpay group) is a Malaysian payment gateway with Basic and Premium plans. Basic has low FPX (1.50%, min RM1) and e-wallet (1.50%) rates, but cards are 2.40% and its pricing page doesn't list in-store payments or a settlement schedule. HitPay charges DuitNow QR at 1.2% and domestic cards at 1.2% + RM1 online and in store, pays cards and FPX in T+1 business days, and adds Tap to Pay with no setup or monthly fee.


*Curlec rates from*[curlec.com/pricing](https://curlec.com/pricing) *, as of 23 Oct 2026. HitPay rates from*[HitPay Malaysia pricing](https://hitpayapp.com/my/pricing) *.*


## Curlec at a glance


-


**Plans:** Basic (RM99 one-time setup, per Curlec's FAQ), Premium (RM999 one-time setup) and Enterprise (for RM1M+/month volume), all with "No annual fee".


-


**Products on the pricing page:** Payment Gateway, Subscriptions, Payouts.

Curlec's "DuitNow Pay" is an online bank-account payment, which is not the same as scanning a DuitNow QR.


## Basic vs Premium: when RM999 pays back


Premium cuts cards from 2.40% to 2.00% and FPX from 1.50% to 1.00%. On cards alone, the RM999 setup fee pays back after about RM250,000 of card sales.


## Curlec pros and cons


-


**Pros:** low FPX and e-wallet rates; no annual fee; Payouts and Subscriptions products on the same account.


-


**Cons:** cards 2.40% on Basic; the page shows "18% GST applicable"; no in-store or settlement schedule on the pricing page.


## Who Curlec suits


Online businesses that mostly take FPX and want subscription billing.


## Curlec alternative: HitPay


DuitNow QR 1.2%, cards 1.2% + RM1 online and in store, FPX and card payouts T+1 business day (other methods T+2), Tap to Pay on iPhone, terminals bought once from MYR 310, one dashboard and one payout. Honest note: Curlec is cheaper on FPX.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### How much does Curlec charge in Malaysia?


On its Basic plan (as of 23 Oct 2026), Razorpay Curlec lists credit and debit cards at 2.40%, foreign cards at 3.30%, FPX at 1.50% (or RM1, whichever is greater), DuitNow Pay at 1.20% (min RM0.30) and e-wallets at 1.50%. Premium lowers these, for example cards to 2.00% and FPX to 1.00% (min RM1).


### Does Curlec have a setup fee?


Yes. Curlec Basic has a one-time setup fee of RM99 (per Curlec's FAQ) and Premium has a RM999 one-time setup fee. There is no annual fee.


### Is Curlec cheaper than HitPay?


On FPX, yes: Curlec Basic lists 1.50% (min RM1) and HitPay 1.8% + RM0.40. On domestic cards, HitPay's 1.2% + RM1 is cheaper than Curlec Basic's 2.40% on orders above about RM84, and cheaper than Curlec Premium's 2.00% above RM125.


### Can I use Curlec in store?


Curlec's pricing page doesn't list in-store terminals or Tap to Pay. HitPay takes cards at 1.2% + RM1 and DuitNow QR at 1.2% in store, on a terminal bought once from MYR 310 or with Tap to Pay on iPhone.


### How fast does HitPay pay out compared with Curlec?


HitPay pays FPX and cards in T+1 business days and other methods in T+2 business days. Curlec doesn't publish a settlement schedule on its pricing page, so ask Curlec directly.
